faqs.q: When is it urgent to call a 24-hour emergency electrician?
faqs.a: Call right away if you have to reset the breaker often, lights dim or flicker when appliances start, you smell electrical burning, the breaker box is hot or humming, or you have seen sparks, smoke or melted wiring.

faqs.q: How will I know when to replace my breaker box?
faqs.a: Frequent breaker trips, an older home with an outdated system, melted or heavily worn wiring, strange noises from the panel, flickering lights, power surges when appliances start, or appliances that overheat. Contact us for an inspection and we will tell you which it is.

faqs.q: What is the lifespan of a breaker panel?
faqs.a: According to the Consumer Product Safety Commission, a breaker panel's average lifespan is typically between 30 and 40 years, and humidity can shorten it.

faqs.q: How often should my electrical panel be inspected?
faqs.a: Usually once every three to five years, though it depends on the age of the home and how much the system is being asked to supply.

faqs.q: Can I do the electrical work on my own?
faqs.a: DIY electrical work is not recommended. There is a real risk of electrocution, improper work and fire, which is why electricians go through rigorous training and licensing first.

faqs.q: What parts of my home should be GFCI protected?
faqs.a: GFCI equipment should be installed in all wet locations, including garages, around sinks, kitchens and bathrooms.

faqs.q: Do I need a surge protector?
faqs.a: Yes. A surge from lightning or the power station enters the house without one, and it can destroy televisions, computers and anything else plugged in. A surge protector blocks the excess current or shorts it to ground.

faqs.q: What can I do to prevent electrical emergencies?
faqs.a: Whole-home surge protection, a backup generator, GFCIs, regular maintenance by a licensed electrician, no damaged or indoor-rated extension cords outdoors, and nothing overloaded or left near water.

faqs.q: Is your work covered by a warranty?
faqs.a: Most installations and electrical repairs come with a warranty, and we are always happy to go through the details specific to your project.

faqs.q: Do you take on small electrical jobs?
faqs.a: Yes. No job is too small, from fixing an outlet to installing a new light switch.

A ground-fault circuit interrupter is a breaker built into an outlet, with test and reset buttons on its face. It cuts the power the moment it detects an improper flow of current, which is what stops a shock before it reaches you.

faqs.q: Is there a difference between my breaker panel and my old fuse panel?
faqs.a: Yes. Both are designed to trip on an electrical overload, but a breaker panel can be reset while a fuse has to be replaced after every trip.

faqs.q: Why does my circuit breaker panel feel hot?
faqs.a: Usually the panel is at its limit for current and needs upgrading, or it has gone bad and needs replacing. A hot panel with flickering lights often means a bad breaker, and it is common in a faulty brand like Federal Pacific Stab-Lok, so call the emergency electrician rather than waiting.

faqs.q: How do I reset my main breaker?
faqs.a: Turn off each breaker switch in the panel one at a time, find the main breaker outside near the electric meter, flip the main switch off and back on twice and leave it on without touching the meter, then switch the breakers in the panel back on. If the power does not come back, contact us.

faqs.q: Do commercial electricians need unique licensing or certifications?
faqs.a: In Texas an electrician is not required to hold any additional licensing or training to take on commercial work, which is exactly why experience and reputation matter so much when you choose one.

faqs.q: What is the difference between residential and commercial electrical?
faqs.a: Residential work is done in someone's home and commercial work in an office or other professional setting, usually on a much larger scale. We do both, which gives us a fine-tuned understanding of each.

faqs.q: How can I prevent electrical fires?
faqs.a: Have a licensed electrician inspect the home to find and repair any malfunction, and upgrade the electrical equipment when it is recommended.

faqs.q: Why is my breaker box making a buzzing or humming noise?
faqs.a: Buzzing or humming from the breaker box points to a defective system. Get an electrician out quickly and have it replaced before the other electrical components take any harm.
